name: Big Oat Jar with chia
wt: 440 g jar + banana on the side
base: 70 g dry oats + 10 g chia + banana
ing: rolled oats 70 g; cottage cheese 2% 175 g; milk 2% 100 g; chia seeds 10 g; blueberries 75 g; banana 100 g; peanut butter 8 g
steps: Stir oats, cottage cheese, milk and chia together in a 32 oz jar.
Top with the blueberries and peanut butter. Do not stir them in.
Fridge at least 8 hours — chia is still gritty at four. Banana eaten on the side in the car.
store: Batch four at once, keeps 4 days. Day four is noticeably stiffer — loosen with a splash of milk.
note: Flax version: swap 10 g ground flax for the chia and drop peanut butter to 6 g. Use ground, never whole.

name: Protein Pancakes
ing: rolled oats 55 g; cottage cheese 2% 120 g; egg 50 g; protein powder 10 g; peanut butter 10 g; banana 110 g; maple syrup 25 g; blueberries 75 g
steps: Blend oats, cottage cheese, egg and protein powder smooth, 45 seconds.
Nonstick pan or griddle at medium, lightly greased. Quarter-cup pancakes, 2–3 min a side.
Top with peanut butter, sliced banana, blueberries and the syrup.
store: Batter keeps 3 days blended. Cooked pancakes freeze and go straight into a toaster.
note: Cook these Sunday and freeze them if they are for a Thursday or Friday — three days is the fridge limit.

name: Greek Yogurt Bowl
base: 25 g Three Wishes + 25 g rice crisps + banana
ing: greek yogurt nonfat 200 g; three wishes cereal 25 g; one degree brown rice crisps 25 g; blueberries 100 g; banana 120 g; peanut butter 27 g; honey 15 g
steps: Yogurt into the bowl, cereal and fruit over.
Peanut butter and honey last.
store: Assemble fresh — cereal goes soft within the hour.
note: The 25 g of peanut butter and the full banana are what close this against slot. Weigh both; eyeballed, this bowl runs 7 g fat and 16 g carb short.

name: Banana-PB Overnight Oats
ing: rolled oats 70 g; greek yogurt nonfat 170 g; milk 2% 100 g; banana 130 g; peanut butter 20 g; honey 10 g
steps: Mash half the banana into the oats, yogurt and milk.
Slice the rest on top with the peanut butter and honey.
Fridge at least 4 hours.
store: Four days in the jar is the outer limit and it stiffens by then. Build it two nights ahead, not on Sunday.
note: Same jar format as B1, completely different texture — creamy rather than curdy. This is the cottage-cheese-fatigue option.

name: Freezer Breakfast Burrito
ing: flour tortilla 72 g; egg 75 g; potato 170 g; cheddar 10 g; salsa 40 g; greek yogurt nonfat 150 g; banana 110 g
steps: Microwave the diced potato 7 min until just tender, then griddle over medium-high 8–10 min to crisp, seasoning with cumin, garlic powder, paprika and salt as it goes.
Scramble the eggs soft and pull them 30 seconds early — they finish cooking on reheat.
Warm the tortillas 15 seconds so they roll without cracking. Fill with potato, egg, cheddar, salsa. Roll tight, seam-side down, wrap individually in foil then a freezer bag.
From frozen: unwrap the foil, 2 min in the microwave on a paper towel, or 8 min in the air fryer at 350 °F.
store: Freezer 2 months, fridge 4 days.
note: Yogurt and banana on the side are part of the serving, not extras — the burrito alone is well short of slot.

name: Blueberry Baked Oatmeal, 2 squares
ing: rolled oats 75 g; egg 25 g; milk 2% 75 g; greek yogurt nonfat 110 g; banana 65 g; blueberries 75 g; peanut butter 15 g; honey 15 g; protein powder 8 g
steps: Oven 350 °F. Whisk eggs, milk, yogurt, mashed banana, honey and melted peanut butter.
Stir in oats, protein powder, baking powder, cinnamon and a pinch of salt. Fold in the blueberries.
Into a greased 9×13, bake 35–40 min until the centre is set and the top springs back.
Cool completely before cutting — warm oatmeal crumbles. Cut into 8.
store: Fridge 5 days, freezer 3 months. 45 seconds from the fridge, 90 from frozen.
note: The most hands-off breakfast here — bake once and there are no morning decisions for most of a week. A serving is two squares plus 60 g of yogurt spooned over.

name: Cottage Cheese French Toast
ing: sourdough 100 g; egg 50 g; cottage cheese 2% 140 g; milk 2% 50 g; maple syrup 20 g; blueberries 100 g; peanut butter 12 g; banana 40 g
steps: Blend the cottage cheese, egg and milk smooth, 30 seconds. Blending is what makes it a custard rather than scrambled egg on bread.
Soak each slice 20 seconds a side. Thick-cut sourdough holds; thin sandwich bread collapses.
Griddle or nonstick at medium, lightly greased, 3 min a side to deep golden.
Fruit, peanut butter and syrup over.
store: Best fresh. Cooked slices keep 2 days and re-crisp in a toaster oven.
note: The weekend one — this is breakfast sat down, not breakfast in the car.

name: Oats Overnight, cottage cheese base
ing: oats overnight packet 76 g; cottage cheese 2% 120 g; rolled oats 20 g; frozen blueberries 75 g; peanut butter 12 g; banana 120 g
steps: Blend the cottage cheese with 120 ml water until completely smooth, 30–45 seconds. Skip this and you get curds suspended in oats.
Blended base into the shaker, then the packet, the extra oats and the peanut butter.
Frozen blueberries in last — they thaw overnight and release liquid, which loosens the thicker base back to spoonable.
Shake hard 20 seconds, fridge overnight. If it is still too thick, thin with water, not milk.
store: Overnight. Blend a week of cottage-cheese base at once — it holds 4 days.
note: Everything here except the pouch and the added oats gives 46 g of carbohydrate, so the pouch plus the oats have to supply about 53 g to reach slot. This build carries the pouch at 54.3 g carbohydrate per 100 g — read your own pouch’s panel and adjust: 10 g of dry oats adds 6.8 g of carbohydrate, so for every 7 g the pouch is short, add 10 g of oats. ⚠️ Protein is unresolved — this build costs the pouch at 26.3 g protein per 100 g, the value Close the Carbs ships; the custom food entered by hand says 10.7. Read the panel before trusting this row.

name: Saturday run window
base: 40 g dry oats pre · honey during · yogurt bowl post
ing: rolled oats 40 g; milk 2% 100 g; banana 130 g; honey 25 g; greek yogurt nonfat 200 g; three wishes cereal 13 g; one degree brown rice crisps 12 g; blueberries 75 g; peanut butter 19 g
steps: 60–75 min before the run: 40 g dry oats, 100 ml milk, 100 g banana, 5 g honey. Low fat, low fibre.
From about 45 minutes in: 15–20 g of carbohydrate an hour — 20 g honey and 30 g banana, or an equivalent gel.
Within 45 min of finishing: 200 g Greek yogurt, 13 g Three Wishes + 12 g rice crisps, 75 g blueberries, 15 g peanut butter.
store: Assemble the pre-run bowl the night before; the post-run bowl fresh.
note: 117 g of carbohydrate does not go on one plate, and Saturday is the only morning breakfast is not your post-lift meal. Presenting this as a single serving is the failure mode.

name: Chipotle-Honey Chicken & Rice Bowl
ing: chicken breast 133 g; white rice dry 50 g; black beans canned 50 g; corn frozen 40 g; bell pepper 60 g; olive oil 4 g; honey 8 g; chipotle in adobo 5 g; lime juice 10 g; cheddar 10 g; pico de gallo 50 g; avocado 35 g
steps: Oven 425 °F. Cube the chicken, toss with the oil, cumin, garlic powder, paprika and salt. Diced pepper on the same pan. Roast 18 min.
Rice 1:1.75 by volume — 18 min covered on low, then 10 min off the heat with the lid on.
Whisk the honey, chipotle and lime into a glaze, pour over the chicken, back in 5 min to 165 °F and caramelised at the edges.
Layer rice, beans, corn, pepper, chicken, cheddar. Pico in a separate cup.
store: Fridge 4 days. Avocado cut morning-of, never Sunday.
note: Low smell, good cold or hot.

name: Greek Orzo Salad + Turkey Meatballs
ing: ground turkey 93/7 136 g; panko 13 g; egg 20 g; orzo dry 65 g; cucumber 100 g; cherry tomatoes 100 g; red onion 20 g; kalamata olives 8 g; feta 15 g; olive oil 4 g; lemon juice 15 g; garlic 5 g; chickpeas canned 50 g
steps: Oven 425 °F. Mix turkey, panko, egg, half the garlic, oregano, salt and pepper. Do not overwork. Roll 30 g meatballs.
Bake 16–18 min to 165 °F. Do not sear — baked meatballs hold their texture cold, seared ones go greasy in the fridge.
Orzo 8–9 min al dente in well-salted water. Drain, rinse briefly cold, spread on a tray to cool.
Whisk oil, lemon, remaining garlic and oregano. Taste it cold and push the salt and acid further than feels right — chilling flattens both.
Toss the cooled orzo with cucumber, tomato and onion. Meatballs, olives and feta on top.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas well and fold them in with the vegetables. They are the fibre in this bowl — orzo, cucumber and tomato carry almost none between them.
store: Fridge 4 days. Do not reheat — cucumber goes limp and orzo tightens. Meatballs freeze 2 months.
note: Zero office smell and the most fork-friendly item in the bank. Chickpeas added 19 Sep: 4.9 g of fibre to 8.7 for 50 g of beans, and it is the difference between this lunch holding to 3:30 and not.

name: Chicken Burrito Bowl
ing: chicken breast 123 g; white rice dry 58 g; black beans canned 80 g; cheddar 15 g; pico de gallo 60 g; avocado 45 g; olive oil 4 g; lime juice 10 g
steps: Warm the diced chicken through with cumin, chili powder, garlic powder and lime.
Warm the beans and drain them well so they don't water the container.
Layer rice, chicken, beans, cheese. Pico and avocado added morning-of.
store: Fridge 4 days, good cold or reheated.
note: The chicken went up with Revision 4 — 89 g cooked instead of 79. The rice did not move; carbohydrate is untouched by the redistribution.

name: Mediterranean Chicken & Couscous
ing: chicken breast 120 g; pearl couscous dry 65 g; chickpeas canned 50 g; cucumber 80 g; cherry tomatoes 80 g; feta 20 g; kalamata olives 12 g; olive oil 8 g; lemon juice 15 g
steps: Bake the chicken at 400 °F, 22–25 min to 165 °F. Rest, then slice.
Cook the couscous per package, rinse briefly and cool so it doesn't clump.
Whisk oil, lemon, zest and oregano. Toss with couscous, chickpeas, cucumber and tomato.
Chicken, feta and olives over.
store: Fridge 4–5 days. Best cold.
note: One of the three strongest zero-smell options, alongside L2 and L6.

name: Turkey Pesto Pasta Salad
ing: pasta dry 80 g; ground turkey 93/7 111 g; pesto 18 g; greek yogurt nonfat 40 g; cherry tomatoes 100 g; mozzarella 20 g; spinach 20 g; lemon juice 10 g; chickpeas canned 50 g
steps: Brown the turkey, season well, cool.
Pasta al dente, drain, rinse cold.
Thin the pesto with the Greek yogurt and lemon — that is what lets 18 g dress a whole bowl instead of 40 g.
Toss everything together.
Chickpeas drained, rinsed and tossed through at the end. Pesto clings to them better than it does to the pasta.
store: Fridge 4 days. Cold only, zero smell.
note: Chickpeas added 19 Sep — this was the lowest-fibre lunch in the bank at 4.7 g, which is what refined pasta plus lean turkey gets you. Now 8.4.

name: BBQ Chicken & Baked Potato Bowl
ing: chicken breast 129 g; potato 260 g; bbq sauce 35 g; cheddar 15 g; corn frozen 50 g; red onion 25 g; olive oil 9 g; greek yogurt nonfat 30 g
steps: Oven 425 °F. Cube the potato, toss with oil and salt, roast 28–30 min.
Chicken on the same pan for the last 18 min.
Shred the chicken and toss it with the BBQ sauce.
Build: potato, chicken, corn, onion, cheddar, yogurt on top in place of sour cream.
store: Fridge 4 days. Eat hot.
note: The one lunch that needs a microwave, and it carries a BBQ smell — save it for a day you are not in a small shared kitchen.

name: Adult Lunchable
ing: deli turkey 134 g; cheddar 25 g; whole-grain crackers 40 g; egg 50 g; grapes 100 g; cucumber 80 g; cherry tomatoes 80 g; pretzels 20 g; baby carrots 80 g; sugar snap peas 60 g
steps: Boil the eggs 12 min, straight into an ice bath, peel.
Portion into bento containers.
Crackers and pretzels in their own compartment so they stay crisp.
Carrots and snap peas raw in their own compartment. They are not garnish — they are 140 g of the box and most of its fibre.
store: Fridge 5 days — the longest keeper in the lunch set.
note: The original version of this was 33 g of carbohydrate under slot: it read as complete because it had five components, but four of them were protein, fat or vegetables. The crackers, weighed grapes and pretzels fixed the carbohydrate; the carrots and snap peas added 19 Sep fixed the fibre, 5.3 g to 9.1.

name: Turkey & Provolone on Sourdough + Grapes
ing: deli turkey 150 g; sourdough 100 g; provolone 25 g; mayonnaise 10 g; dijon mustard 8 g; romaine 20 g; cherry tomatoes 40 g; cucumber 60 g; grapes 100 g; baby carrots 80 g; sugar snap peas 60 g
steps: Mayo and Dijon edge to edge on both slices — fat is the moisture barrier.
Provolone, turkey, romaine.
Tomato in a separate cup, added at lunch. That is what makes a sandwich soggy, not the mustard.
Carrots and snap peas raw, bagged separately. With L21 retired this sandwich carries the bread lane on its own, so it needs to be the good one.
store: 3 days assembled, 5 days as components.
note: This was the only lunch in the August audit that cleared its carbohydrate slot, and it cleared because it was the only one built on bread. Bread alone does not keep you full, though — 4.8 g of fibre was the lowest of any sandwich. Raw veg added 19 Sep takes it to 8.7.

name: Bruschetta Chicken + Sourdough
ing: chicken breast 116 g; sourdough 110 g; cherry tomatoes 130 g; mozzarella 20 g; olive oil 8 g; balsamic vinegar 10 g; garlic 5 g; basil 5 g; grapes 60 g; chickpeas canned 40 g
steps: Season and bake the chicken at 400 °F, 20–22 min to 165 °F.
Macerate the chopped tomato with garlic, basil, oil and balsamic for at least 20 minutes. This is the whole recipe.
Toast the sourdough fresh each morning — packing it pre-toasted does not work.
Chickpeas drained and marinated with the tomatoes — they take on the garlic and balsamic in the same 20 minutes.
store: Chicken and topping keep 4 days, separately. Toast day-of.
note: Was 9 g short of slot before the sourdough went to 110 g. Chickpeas added 19 Sep for fibre, 5.0 g to 8.0, marinated with the bruschetta rather than added as a side.

name: No-Cook Mezze Box
ing: whole-wheat pita 75 g; hummus 35 g; chickpeas canned 50 g; feta 25 g; cucumber 100 g; cherry tomatoes 100 g; kalamata olives 12 g; deli turkey 144 g
steps: Everything into a bento.
Pita cut into wedges, hummus in its own cup.
store: Fridge 4 days.
note: The pita is the base. Treating hummus and chickpeas as the carbohydrate is what left the original 10 g short.

name: Steak & Potato Salad
ing: sirloin steak 126 g; potato 340 g; olive oil 8 g; dijon mustard 12 g; greek yogurt nonfat 40 g; parmesan 10 g; red onion 25 g; cherry tomatoes 80 g; romaine 40 g; lemon juice 10 g
steps: Boil the potatoes whole in salted water 18–20 min, then quarter. Boiling them whole is what keeps them from going waterlogged.
Dress them while still warm — cold potatoes will not take dressing.
Sear the steak 3–4 min a side, rest 5 min, slice thin against the grain.
Fold everything together with the romaine last.
store: Fridge 4 days. Good cold — the steak stays tender because it is sliced thin into a dressed salad.
note: 265 g of cooked potato is roughly double what a potato salad normally carries. That is the point.

name: Chicken, Wild Rice & Roasted Squash
ing: chicken breast 141 g; wild rice dry 45 g; butternut squash 180 g; olive oil 9 g; dried cranberries 15 g; sliced almonds 8 g; spinach 40 g; balsamic vinegar 10 g
steps: Wild rice takes 45–50 minutes — start it first.
Squash in 2 cm cubes at 425 °F, 25 min. Chicken on the same pan the last 18.
Toss with spinach, cranberries, almonds and balsamic once everything has cooled.
store: Fridge 4 days. Good cold or reheated.
note: The cranberries carry 12 g of carbohydrate on their own, which is why the rice can stay at 45 g dry.

name: Chicken, Sweet Potato & Black Bean Bowl
ing: chicken breast 133 g; sweet potato 250 g; black beans canned 70 g; olive oil 8 g; avocado 35 g; salsa 50 g; cheddar 10 g; lime juice 10 g
steps: Sweet potato in 2 cm cubes at 425 °F, 25 min.
Chicken alongside for the last 18 min, seasoned with cumin and chili powder.
Build with the beans, salsa, cheddar and lime.
store: Fridge 4 days, reheats well. Avocado day-of.
note: Was 15 g short of slot — the worst of the August six. 188 g of roasted sweet potato is what fixed it.

name: Honey-Mustard Chicken & Farro Salad
ing: farro dry 55 g; chicken breast 130 g; apple 90 g; spinach 40 g; red onion 20 g; feta 18 g; sliced almonds 8 g; dijon mustard 12 g; honey 14 g; olive oil 4 g; lemon juice 10 g
steps: Farro in salted boiling water 25–28 min to chewy. Drain and cool.
Season the chicken, bake at 400 °F 20–22 min to 165 °F, rest, dice.
Whisk Dijon, honey, oil and lemon. Toss everything.
store: Fridge 4 days, cold only, zero smell.
note: Farro is the one grain here that does not go stodgy — it holds its bite four days where rice and pasta don't. Put it on Thursday and Friday.

name: Chicken Tinga Rice Bowl
ing: chicken breast 118 g; white rice dry 58 g; crushed tomatoes 90 g; chipotle in adobo 12 g; onion 50 g; olive oil 7 g; black beans canned 50 g; cotija 12 g; greek yogurt nonfat 30 g; avocado 35 g; lime juice 8 g
steps: Poach or bake the chicken, then shred it. Shredding rather than dicing is what makes it tinga — it lets the sauce coat everything.
Soften the onion in the oil 6 min, add chipotle and crushed tomato, simmer 10 min, then blend smooth.
Return the shredded chicken to the sauce for 5 minutes.
Over rice with the beans, cotija and yogurt.
store: Fridge 4 days, reheats very well. Freezes 2 months.
note: Avocado day-of.

name: Turkey, Hummus & Roasted Veg Wrap
ing: large tortilla wrap 70 g; deli turkey 162 g; hummus 40 g; roasted red pepper 50 g; zucchini 60 g; spinach 25 g; feta 18 g; grapes 90 g; pretzels 10 g
steps: Roast the zucchini at 425 °F for 15 min and cool it completely before it goes near the wrap.
Hummus spread edge to edge — that is the moisture barrier that stops a made-ahead wrap going limp.
Fill, roll tight, wrap in foil, cut in half at lunch.
store: 3 days wrapped. Cold, zero smell.

name: Hot Honey Turkey & Sweet Potato Bowl
ing: ground turkey 93/7 115 g; sweet potato 240 g; cottage cheese 2% 110 g; avocado 40 g; hot honey 14 g; olive oil 5 g; spinach 30 g; lime juice 8 g
steps: Oven 425 °F. Sweet potato in 2 cm cubes tossed with the olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin and salt. Spread across two pans rather than crowding one — crowded sweet potato steams and is mush by Wednesday. Roast 25 min, tossing once.
Brown the turkey over medium-high with garlic powder and cumin, 8 min, breaking it up fine. Season assertively: this eats cold or barely warm and cold flattens salt.
Cool both completely before boxing. Warm food in a sealed container makes condensation and condensation makes a soggy bowl.
Layer spinach, sweet potato, turkey. Lime over.
Morning-of: cottage cheese spooned on, avocado, and the hot honey drizzled last.
store: Fridge 4 days. Low smell, good cold or reheated.
note: Yours, built from the brief. The cottage cheese goes on cold and does the job sour cream would, at a much better protein-to-fat ratio — and it keeps the bowl from being dry on day three. The honey goes on in the morning; packed Sunday it soaks into the potato and disappears.

name: Hot Honey Chicken & Cheddar Bento
ing: chicken breast 131 g; olive oil 6 g; hot honey 18 g; cheddar 20 g; sourdough 65 g; apple 70 g; grapes 40 g; cucumber 80 g; almonds 8 g; baby carrots 80 g; sugar snap peas 60 g
steps: Oven 425 °F. Chicken in 2 cm cubes tossed with the oil, garlic powder, smoked paprika and salt. Single layer, 18 min to 165 °F. Cool completely.
Cut the sourdough into fingers, not slices — a slice gets crushed in a bento and a finger doesn't. Leave it untoasted; toasted bread goes leathery in a box.
Box the chicken, cheddar, sourdough, cucumber and almonds. Grapes in their own compartment.
Morning-of: slice the apple, and take the hot honey in a small cup to pour over the chicken at lunch.
Carrots and snap peas raw in their own compartment — they also give you something to eat the hot honey with once the chicken is gone.
store: Fridge 4 days. Zero smell, no reheating.
note: The lunchable idea with something actually cooked in it, so it doesn’t read as a snack plate at 1 pm. Glazing the chicken on Sunday means the honey soaks in and the chicken goes tacky — hence the cup. Raw veg added 19 Sep: 5.0 g of fibre to 8.9.

name: Caprese Turkey Bento
ing: deli turkey 154 g; fresh mozzarella 45 g; cherry tomatoes 120 g; balsamic glaze 12 g; sourdough 80 g; olive oil 5 g; grapes 70 g; kalamata olives 12 g; basil 4 g; baby carrots 80 g; sugar snap peas 60 g
steps: Halve the tomatoes, toss with the olive oil, flaky salt and pepper, and let them sit 10 minutes while you box everything else. That brief salting is the difference between caprese and cold tomato.
Roll the turkey into loose bundles rather than folding it flat — it eats with fingers that way.
Sourdough torn into pieces, mozzarella pearls drained well.
Balsamic glaze in its own small cup. Basil torn in the morning, never Sunday — it blackens.
Carrots and snap peas raw alongside. This box was 4.5 g of fibre before them — the lowest in the bank, because mozzarella, turkey and white bread carry none.
store: Fridge 4 days. Zero cooking, zero smell.
note: The fastest lunch in the bank and the one for a Sunday with no prep window. Dressed on Sunday, the mozzarella goes grey-brown by Wednesday and the bread goes purple. Raw veg added 19 Sep.

name: Yogurt, cereal, banana & PB
base: 13 g Three Wishes + 12 g rice crisps + banana
ing: greek yogurt nonfat 80 g; three wishes cereal 13 g; one degree brown rice crisps 12 g; banana 45 g; peanut butter 12 g
steps: Yogurt, cereal, sliced banana, peanut butter.
store: Assemble fresh.
note: Half the yogurt it used to carry. Doubles as Wednesday pre-run fuel — eat it 60–90 min before; if the run is inside 45 minutes drop the peanut butter to 6 g and add 20 g more banana.

name: Cottage cheese, pineapple & crackers
ing: cottage cheese 2% 110 g; pineapple 110 g; whole-grain crackers 12 g; cashews 10 g
steps: Cottage cheese in the tub, pineapple over.
Crackers and cashews in a separate bag so they stay crisp.
store: 2 days assembled.

name: Turkey, pretzels & grapes
ing: deli turkey 60 g; pretzels 22 g; grapes 60 g; almonds 11 g
steps: Roll the turkey, bag the rest separately.
store: 2 days.
note: No spoon, no smell, no cheese — useful on a day already heavy on dairy.

name: Apple, peanut butter & a yogurt cup
ing: apple 140 g; peanut butter 14 g; greek yogurt nonfat 110 g; honey 6 g
steps: Honey stirred through the yogurt.
Apple sliced at your desk, peanut butter for dipping.
store: Slice the apple day-of.
note: The plainest thing in the bank and probably the one you will reach for most. This is what a snack is supposed to look like.

name: Desk-drawer kit
ing: pretzels 30 g; turkey jerky 30 g; almonds 12 g
steps: Keep a bag of pretzels, a bag of jerky and a bag of almonds permanently in your desk. Restock monthly.
Weigh them into small bags on Sunday if you want it exact.
store: Shelf-stable. Nothing here needs a fridge or a shaker.
note: At 24 g of protein this kit needed a scoop of powder and a shaker bottle. At 15 it is three bags of food. That is the clearest single argument for the redistribution — the option that exists for the day you forgot to pack anything just got much easier to actually keep stocked. Weigh the pretzels: a poured handful is anywhere from 20 to 60 g, which is 30 g of carbohydrate.

name: PB & honey on sourdough + yogurt
ing: sourdough 42 g; peanut butter 14 g; greek yogurt nonfat 90 g; honey 4 g
steps: Make the sandwich in the morning and wrap it.
Small cup of yogurt alongside — no shaker needed now.
store: Same day.
note: Used to need a scoop of protein powder to reach slot. It doesn't any more.

name: Hot honey cottage cheese & pretzels
ing: cottage cheese 2% 110 g; pretzels 25 g; hot honey 6 g; almonds 8 g
steps: Cottage cheese in the tub, hot honey over it, crack black pepper on top.
Pretzels and almonds in a separate bag — dip them rather than mixing them in, or they are soft by 3:30.
store: Tub the night before; dry things separate.
note: Eats like a treat. 110 g of cottage cheese is half a normal tub — it now reads as a dip rather than a meal.

name: Popcorn, jerky & grapes
ing: air-popped popcorn 20 g; turkey jerky 30 g; grapes 40 g; almonds 12 g
steps: Air-pop the corn at home — 20 g of kernels is about three and a half cups popped.
Salt it, do not butter it; the fat slot is small.
store: Popcorn holds 2 days sealed.
note: By a distance the biggest-looking snack here, which matters on a day you are actually hungry rather than just due.

name: Chocolate cottage cheese pudding
ing: cottage cheese 2% 110 g; cocoa powder 4 g; honey 8 g; banana 40 g; graham crackers 9 g; peanut butter 8 g
steps: Blend the cottage cheese, cocoa, honey and peanut butter completely smooth — 45 seconds, and smooth is the whole point; grainy cocoa cottage cheese is unpleasant.
Into a tub, banana sliced on top.
Graham crackers in a separate bag, crumbled over at 3:30.
store: Blends fine on Sunday and holds 4 days — it thickens slightly, which is an improvement.
note: The closest thing here to dessert.

name: Chia pudding, granola & berries
ing: greek yogurt nonfat 110 g; milk 2% 50 g; chia seeds 7 g; granola 24 g; strawberries 80 g
steps: Stir the yogurt, milk and chia together. Fridge overnight — chia wants 8 hours, not 4.
Strawberries sliced in.
Granola in a separate bag, over the top at 3:30 or it dissolves.
store: Batch four at once, holds 4 days.
note: Make it Sunday alongside the lunches and the snack slot is decided for half the week.

name: Everything-bagel cottage cheese rice cakes
ing: rice cakes 24 g; cottage cheese 2% 110 g; cherry tomatoes 60 g; avocado 32 g; everything bagel seasoning 2 g
steps: Cottage cheese, halved tomatoes and seasoning in a tub; avocado added in the morning.
Rice cakes in a separate bag — top them at your desk, because spread ahead they are soft within the hour.
store: Tub holds 2 days; avocado the morning you eat it.

name: Mango, yogurt & cashews
ing: greek yogurt nonfat 130 g; dried mango 16 g; cashews 15 g; pineapple 60 g
steps: Yogurt in the tub with the fresh pineapple stirred through.
Mango and cashews in a separate bag — mango goes leathery-soft sitting in yogurt.
store: 2 days.
note: Buy dried mango with no added sugar. The sweetened kind is nearly double the carbohydrate per gram and would put this well over slot. Weigh it — 16 g is a small amount.

name: Edamame & apple
ing: shelled edamame frozen 130 g; apple 110 g; pretzels 5 g
steps: Steam or microwave the edamame 3 min from frozen, cool completely, salt it well.
Bag it with the sliced apple.
store: 3 days. Good cold, zero smell.
note: The only option with no dairy in it at all — the one for a heavy-yogurt day.

name: Berry smoothie in a thermos
ing: greek yogurt nonfat 90 g; frozen mixed berries 122 g; milk 2% 80 g; almond butter 8 g; rolled oats 10 g
steps: Blend everything, 45 seconds. The oats are what give it body — without them it drinks thin and you are hungry at four.
Into an insulated bottle in the morning; it holds cold until mid-afternoon.
store: Blend the morning of. Overnight it separates and the oats swell.
note: A different format rather than a different flavour, and that matters on a day when chewing another packed thing is the problem.

name: Stuffed dates & jerky
ing: medjool dates 30 g; peanut butter 12 g; turkey jerky 33 g; almonds 3 g
steps: Split the dates, remove the stones, fill with peanut butter, press an almond in. Flaky salt if you have it.
Jerky alongside.
store: Dates keep for weeks. Stuff a week’s worth at once and keep them in the drawer.
note: The second shelf-stable option, and it no longer needs a shaker either. 30 g is about one and a bit — weigh them, medjools vary enormously.

name: Caprese plate
ing: fresh mozzarella 40 g; cherry tomatoes 100 g; sourdough 45 g; deli turkey 20 g; balsamic glaze 5 g
steps: Halve the tomatoes and salt them lightly.
Sourdough torn into pieces, mozzarella pearls drained, turkey rolled.
Balsamic glaze in its own small cup — dressed ahead, the mozzarella goes grey.
store: 2 days.
note: New at the smaller size. At 24 g of protein a caprese snack was impossible without a pile of cheese that blew the fat slot; at 15 it works.

name: Parmesan, turkey & pretzels
ing: parmesan snack cheese 21 g; deli turkey 30 g; pretzels 22 g; grapes 70 g; baby carrots 60 g
steps: One BelGioioso Power-Full parmesan piece, the turkey rolled into loose bundles, everything else bagged separately.
Pretzels stay in their own bag until 3:30 or they soften against the grapes.
store: Assemble the night before; the cheese keeps its texture 2 days out of the fridge and a week in it.
note: The parmesan is a hard cheese, not a spoonable one — that is the whole point of it here. One 21 g piece carries 7 g of protein and 6 g of fat, so it does most of the work of a yogurt cup without being a yogurt cup, and the turkey closes the gap rather than a second piece of cheese doing it. Two pieces would put fat 4 g over slot. Carbohydrate runs 6 g above slot, which is the right direction.

name: Turkey stick, apple & crackers
ing: turkey snack stick 33 g; whole-grain crackers 25 g; apple 120 g; almonds 5 g
steps: One Chomps turkey stick, crackers and almonds in the drawer permanently; apple sliced at your desk.
Nothing here needs a fridge except the apple, and the apple does not really need one either.
store: Stick and crackers keep for months. Restock monthly alongside the desk-drawer kit.
note: No dairy at all and no spoon — the second option in the bank you can build entirely from a desk drawer, and unlike S6 it does not lean on jerky sugar to get there. A turkey stick is 12 g of protein for 3.5 g of fat, which is the leanest protein-per-gram of anything shelf-stable here. Weigh the crackers: a sleeve poured by hand is easily double 25 g.

name: Protein bar & apple
ing: protein bar high fibre 45 g; apple 130 g
steps: Keep two in your bag. That is the recipe.
store: Months. This is the option for a day that goes sideways.
note: Honest assessment: this is the worst macro fit in the snack bank and it is here because a bar in your bag beats a skipped snack. An IQBAR runs 12 g of fat against an 8 g slot and only 13 g of carbohydrate against 30, so the apple is not a garnish — it is most of the carbohydrate. It still lands 2.6 g under on protein, which is left alone deliberately. The bigger flag is fibre: one bar carries 10 g, nearly all of it chicory-root type that ferments fast. Given slow transit that is a lot to arrive at once, so treat this as the travel option rather than the Tuesday one, and do not run it on a day with a bean-based lunch.

name: Peanut butter power balls
ing: rolled oats 32 g; peanut butter 10 g; honey 10 g; protein powder 12 g
steps: Scale every line by the number of servings you are making — six servings is eighteen balls and about a week and a half.
Stir the oats and protein powder together dry first. Powder added to wet mix clumps and you get chalky pockets.

Warm the peanut butter and honey together 20 seconds in the microwave so they pour, then stir them through. The mix should hold when squeezed; if it crumbles add water a teaspoon at a time, never more oil.
Chill the mix 20 minutes before rolling — warm mix sticks to your hands and you lose a third of it.
Roll into 22 g balls, three to a serving. A scale is faster than eyeballing and the whole point is that a serving is a known quantity.
store: Fridge 2 weeks, freezer 3 months. They go rock-hard frozen — take a serving out the night before.
note: Exactly on slot at 15.3 / 8.0 / 33.1, which is the tightest fit of any snack here, and it is the only make-ahead option that is not a tub. The ratio matters: 10 g of peanut butter per serving looks mean, and it is what keeps fat at slot — the usual internet ratio is nearly double that and lands 12 g of fat, which is where a power ball quietly becomes a fat bomb. The honey does the binding that the extra peanut butter would have. Chocolate chips would add about 3 g of fat per serving; if you want them, that is the trade.

name: Honey-Garlic Salmon, Jasmine Rice, Broccolini
ing: salmon 128 g; jasmine rice dry 70 g; broccolini 150 g; olive oil 5 g; honey 15 g; soy sauce low sodium 15 g; garlic 6 g; edamame frozen 70 g
steps: Oven 425 °F. Rice on: 1:1.5 by volume, 15 min covered low plus 10 min rest.
Whisk the honey, soy and garlic into a glaze.
Broccolini tossed with oil, salt and pepper on a sheet pan. Push to one side, salmon on the other, brushed generously with the glaze.
Roast 12–14 min until the salmon flakes at the thickest point and the broccolini is charring at the tips. Lemon and the rest of the glaze at the end.
Edamame from frozen, steamed 3 min and salted, tipped into the bowl at the end. Broccolini alone left this at 4.9 g of fibre.
store: Fridge 3 days. Salmon is good cold over the rice the next day.
note: Full batch for two: 340 g salmon, 150 g dry rice, 350 g broccolini, 12 g oil, 30 g honey, 30 g soy, 12 g garlic.

name: Blackstone Smash Burgers + Griddled Wedges
ing: ground beef 90/10 119 g; burger bun 60 g; american cheese 15 g; potato 230 g; olive oil 5 g; ketchup 15 g; onion 30 g; romaine 25 g; cherry tomatoes 40 g
steps: Par-cook the wedges first — microwave the cut potatoes 6–7 min until just fork-tender, then toss with oil, paprika, garlic powder and salt. This is the whole trick.
Blackstone at medium-high. Wedges down cut-side first, 10–12 min turning twice, then move to a cool zone.
Divide the beef into 85 g balls — two thin patties per burger beats one thick one for crust. Griddle screaming hot, ball down, smash flat and hard for 10 seconds, salt.
90 seconds, then flip: the crust releases when it is ready, not before. Cheese on immediately, 60 seconds more.
Toast the cut buns in the beef fat, 45 seconds. Build.
store: Best fresh. Cooked patties keep 3 days — reheat in a dry pan, never the microwave. Wedges do not survive reheating.
note: Full batch for two: 340 g beef, 2 buns, 2 slices cheese, 550 g potatoes, 12 g oil, 30 g ketchup, 60 g onion, 60 g romaine, 90 g tomato.

name: Pineapple Chicken Stir Fry + Jasmine Rice
ing: chicken breast 118 g; jasmine rice dry 45 g; pineapple 90 g; bell pepper 80 g; sugar snap peas 60 g; red onion 40 g; cashews 22 g; soy sauce low sodium 20 g; honey 10 g; sesame oil 9 g; cornstarch 4 g; garlic 6 g; ginger 5 g; broccoli 100 g
steps: Rice on first: 15 min covered low plus 10 min rest.
Toss the sliced chicken with half the cornstarch — the velveting step, and it is why the chicken stays tender at high heat.
Whisk the sauce: soy, honey, rice vinegar, remaining cornstarch, 30 ml water.
Wok on high with half the sesame oil. Chicken in a single layer, do not stir for 90 seconds, then toss 2–3 min and remove.
Remaining oil, garlic and ginger 30 seconds, then pepper, snap peas and onion 3–4 min to crisp-tender. Pineapple 1 min. Chicken back, sauce in, toss 60–90 seconds to gloss. Cashews off the heat.
Broccoli in with the peppers and snap peas, 3–4 min to tender-crisp.
store: Fridge 3 days. Reheats well; the snap peas soften. Keep the cashews separate if you want them crisp.
note: The rice base is smaller here than in other dinners because the pineapple, honey and cashews already carry about 25 g of carbohydrate between them. The slot is still met — do not add rice back without re-checking.

name: Chicken Souvlaki + Greek Lemon Potatoes
ing: chicken breast 118 g; potato 400 g; olive oil 14 g; tzatziki 60 g; cucumber 60 g; cherry tomatoes 60 g; lemon juice 20 g
steps: Marinate first: chicken with olive oil, lemon, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper. Leave 20 min while the potatoes start.
Oven 425 °F. Potato wedges tossed with oil, lemon, garlic and oregano into a baking dish. Pour stock around them, not over, and cover tightly with foil.
Roast covered 25 min. Uncover, toss, roast a further 15–18 min until the liquid has gone and the edges are browned and sticky. That two-stage method is what makes them Greek rather than just roasted.
Chicken on a second pan, 14–16 min to 165 °F, or on the Blackstone 3–4 min a side.
Build with cucumber, tomato and tzatziki spooned over.
store: Fridge 4 days — the best keeper of the Week 7 set. Potatoes re-crisp in the air fryer, 5 min at 400 °F. Tzatziki separately.
note: 312 g of roasted potato on your plate is more starch than any other dinner in the library carries, and it is the cleanest way to hit a 78 g slot without rice.

name: Blackstone Breakfast-for-Dinner
ing: egg 100 g; liquid egg white 42 g; turkey bacon 30 g; sourdough 100 g; butter 4 g; frozen hash browns 150 g; spinach 100 g; cherry tomatoes 120 g; black beans canned 45 g
steps: Blackstone to medium. Turkey bacon first, 4–5 min turning once. Set aside — it renders enough fat to cook the eggs in.
Hash browns into the rendered fat, spread thin, press down and leave 5 minutes undisturbed. Flip in sections, another 4–5 min. Not moving them is the entire technique.
Butter a clear zone and toast the sourdough, 90 seconds a side.
Eggs in the remaining space, 2–3 min.

Blacken the tomatoes cut-side down on the griddle 3 min, wilt the spinach beside them in the last minute, and warm the black beans through. This plate had 2.4 g of fibre without them — the lowest of any dinner here, because eggs, bacon, toast and hash browns carry none at all.
store: Eat fresh. Eggs and toast do not hold — this is the one dinner with no leftover plan, which is why it belongs on a Friday.
note: The library version of this was coded rest-day and landed 37 g short. Both the sourdough and the hash browns are weighed components here, not 'add hash browns for higher-carb days'.

name: Ground Turkey Taco Skillet + Rice
ing: ground turkey 93/7 109 g; white rice dry 65 g; black beans canned 80 g; bell pepper 60 g; onion 40 g; olive oil 4 g; salsa 50 g; cheddar 12 g; avocado 45 g
steps: Rice on: 18 min covered low plus 10 min rest.
Brown the turkey in the oil over medium-high with chili powder, cumin, garlic powder and salt, breaking it up, 8 min to no pink.
Pepper and onion in, 5 min until softened.
Beans and salsa, warm through 2 min. Serve over the rice with cheddar and avocado.
store: Fridge 4 days, reheats well. Avocado always cut day-of.
note: Reserve a portion before plating if you want it for a lunch — easier than trying to save it afterwards.

name: Garlic-Parm Chicken & Crispy Potatoes
ing: chicken breast 97 g; potato 290 g; olive oil 9 g; milk 2% 40 g; light cream cheese 25 g; parmesan 12 g; mozzarella 15 g; garlic 8 g; broccoli 100 g
steps: Toss the chicken cubes with half the oil, garlic, onion powder, dried herbs, paprika, chili flakes and salt. Potato cubes with the other half and the same seasoning.
Air fry separately at 400 °F: potatoes 20–23 min, chicken 16–18 to 165 °F, shaking the baskets halfway. Oven alternative: both at 425 °F, potatoes 28 min, chicken 18.
Sauce: warm the milk, cream cheese and parmesan over low, stirring smooth, 3–4 min. Mozzarella off the heat. Do not boil it or it splits.
Toss the chicken and potatoes through the sauce. Parsley.
Broccoli tossed in with the potatoes for the last 15 min, then through the sauce with everything else.
store: Fridge 4 days. A splash of milk when reheating loosens the sauce.
note: Built at rest-day size — this is the Sunday dinner. On a lifting day it needs about 28 g more dry rice or another 126 g of raw potato.

name: Shrimp Fajita Bowls + Cilantro-Lime Rice
ing: shrimp 140 g; white rice dry 75 g; bell pepper 90 g; onion 50 g; olive oil 8 g; avocado 45 g; pico de gallo 50 g; cheddar 12 g; lime juice 10 g
steps: Rice on: 18 min low plus 10 min rest. Fold lime juice and chopped cilantro through off the heat.
Cast iron or Blackstone on high. Peppers and onion in the oil, 5–6 min until they take colour and still have bite. Push aside.
Shrimp tossed in chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika and garlic powder, 2 min a side to pink and opaque. Stop there — shrimp is ninety seconds from perfect to rubber.
Build: rice, vegetables, shrimp, avocado, pico, cheddar.
store: Fridge 3 days. Reheat the shrimp gently or eat it cold over the rice.
note: The fastest dinner in the bank — this is the one for 6:40 pm with nothing started.

name: Ground Turkey Bolognese over Rigatoni
ing: ground turkey 93/7 100 g; rigatoni dry 70 g; crushed tomatoes 150 g; tomato paste 20 g; onion 40 g; carrot 40 g; celery 30 g; olive oil 7 g; parmesan 12 g; milk 2% 30 g; garlic 6 g
steps: Dice the onion, carrot and celery fine — the finer the dice, the better the sauce. Sweat in the olive oil over medium, 8 min, until soft and sweet.
Garlic 30 seconds. Turkey in, broken up fine, 6–8 min to no pink.
Tomato paste in, 2 min. Cooking the paste out is what gives this depth without a long simmer. Then crushed tomatoes, oregano, bay leaf, salt.
Simmer 20 min uncovered, stirring occasionally. Milk stirred in for the last 5.
Pasta al dente, reserve 100 ml of the water, toss sauce and pasta together in the pan with a splash. Parmesan at the table.
store: The best keeper in the bank — sauce holds 5 days and freezes 3 months. Make a double batch of sauce and two dinners' work is behind you.
note: Use regular semolina pasta. High-protein pasta runs about 9 g less carbohydrate and 6 g more protein at the same dry weight — the wrong direction on both axes at once.

name: Honey-Garlic Chicken Thighs + Sweet Potato
ing: chicken thigh 155 g; sweet potato 280 g; green beans 130 g; olive oil 9 g; honey 15 g; soy sauce low sodium 12 g; garlic 8 g
steps: Oven 425 °F. Sweet potato in 2 cm cubes tossed with oil and salt. Roast 22 min.
Whisk honey, soy, garlic, rice vinegar and red pepper flakes.
Green beans onto the pan, thighs alongside brushed with half the glaze. Roast 15–18 min to 175 °F — thighs want to go past 165, unlike breast; that is where they get tender.
Remaining glaze over at the table.
store: Fridge 4 days, reheats well.
note: The only place in the bank where the protein brings real fat with it, which is why the added oil is low.

name: Blackstone Steak & Loaded Baked Potato
ing: sirloin steak 85 g; potato 380 g; butter 6 g; greek yogurt nonfat 40 g; cheddar 18 g; scallions 10 g; olive oil 4 g; broccoli 120 g
steps: Microwave the potatoes 8–10 min, then finish in a 425 °F oven 15 min for a crisp skin. Straight oven-baking is 55 minutes; this gets the same result inside the weeknight window.
Broccoli tossed in oil, roasted alongside 15 min.
Blackstone screaming hot. Steak salted heavily, 3–4 min a side to medium. Rest 5 minutes — non-negotiable — then slice against the grain.
Split the potatoes, fork the insides up, butter, yogurt, cheddar, scallions, steak over the top.
store: Fridge 3 days. Reheat the steak in short bursts.
note: The steak is deliberately light. Protein is already covered by breakfast and lunch; the potato is doing the work here.

name: Spicy Salmon Rice Bowls with Cucumber
ing: salmon 112 g; jasmine rice dry 80 g; cucumber 100 g; avocado 25 g; edamame frozen 50 g; mayonnaise 4 g; sriracha 10 g; soy sauce low sodium 12 g; sesame seeds 3 g; scallions 10 g; cabbage slaw mix 100 g
steps: Rice on. Season it with a splash of rice vinegar while warm.
Salmon skin-side down in a hot dry pan, 4 min, flip 2–3 min. Or roast at 425 °F for 12 min. Flake into large pieces.
Whisk the mayo, sriracha and soy into a thin sauce. This is a drizzle, not a dressing.
Build: rice, salmon, cucumber, edamame, avocado, sauce, sesame, scallion.
Shredded cabbage raw under the rice — it stays crisp under the sauce where the cucumber goes soft.
store: Fridge 2 days — the shortest here. Good cold the next day.
note: Salmon plus avocado plus mayo runs this to the top of the fat slot. The avocado is at 25 g rather than the usual 45 for exactly that reason — do not add more.

name: Turkey Smash Burger Tacos + Street-Corn Rice
base: 78 g corn tortillas + 99 g cooked rice
ing: ground turkey 93/7 110 g; corn tortillas 78 g; american cheese 15 g; white rice dry 33 g; corn frozen 60 g; cotija 12 g; greek yogurt nonfat 30 g; mayonnaise 4 g; onion 25 g; lime juice 8 g
steps: Rice on. Fold through the corn, cotija, yogurt, a little mayo, chili powder and lime — this is elote in rice form and it is where a third of the carbohydrate lives.
Blackstone or a heavy pan on high. Press 40 g of turkey directly onto each tortilla in a thin layer, meat side down. 2 min until the edges brown and crisp.
Flip so the tortilla toasts, 1 min, cheese on, fold.
Diced onion, cilantro, lime.
store: Components hold 3 days; assemble fresh. The rice is a good bonus lunch base.
note: Burger night and taco night in one, on a lifting day.

name: Pesto Chicken Pasta
ing: chicken breast 80 g; pasta dry 92 g; pesto 20 g; cherry tomatoes 110 g; parmesan 12 g; greek yogurt nonfat 30 g; olive oil 6 g; garlic 6 g; broccoli 150 g
steps: Sear the seasoned chicken 5–6 min a side to 165 °F, rest, slice.
Blister the tomatoes with garlic in the same pan, 3–4 min.
Toss the pasta with the pesto loosened by the Greek yogurt and a splash of pasta water.
Chicken and parmesan over.
Broccoli blanched 2 min in the pasta water before the pasta goes in — one pan, and it takes the pesto as well as the pasta does.
store: Fridge 3 days. Reheat with a splash of water.
note: Dead on slot — the tightest fit in the bank. The old version of this was the highest-fat dinner in the library and still 10 g short on carbohydrate, and it was being reached for whenever fat ran low. That was the wrong instinct: fat is not your gap.

name: Ground Turkey Pasta Bake
ing: ground turkey 93/7 85 g; pasta dry 75 g; marinara 130 g; cottage cheese 2% 40 g; zucchini 80 g; broccoli 80 g; mozzarella 20 g; olive oil 6 g
steps: Brown the turkey, set aside.
Zucchini and broccoli in the oil, 5–7 min tender-crisp.
Blend the marinara with the cottage cheese until smooth — that is the creaminess without cream.
Combine everything, top with mozzarella, bake at 350 °F for 15–20 min, then broil 3 min to brown.
store: Fridge 5 days, freezes 3 months in individual portions. Reheats better than anything else here.
note: Regular pasta, not Barilla Protein Plus. Switching to regular drops 5 g of protein and frees the room for 10 g more dry pasta — protein pasta is solving a problem you do not have.

name: Buffalo Chicken & Sweet Potato Bowl
base: 188 g sweet potato + 84 g cooked rice
ing: chicken breast 110 g; sweet potato 250 g; white rice dry 28 g; buffalo sauce 30 g; greek yogurt nonfat 45 g; blue cheese 18 g; olive oil 11 g; celery 40 g; carrot 40 g; scallions 10 g
steps: Sweet potato in 2 cm cubes at 425 °F, 25 min.
Rice on — a small pot; this is a supporting base, not the main one.
Chicken roasted or griddled to 165 °F, then shredded, not diced. Buffalo sauce clings to shredded chicken and slides off cubes. Toss it hot.
Thin the Greek yogurt with a splash of water and a little blue cheese into a ranch-style drizzle.
Build: sweet potato and rice, chicken, celery, carrot, drizzle, remaining blue cheese, scallion.
store: Fridge 4 days. Reheats well; keep the drizzle separate.
note: Two bases rather than one, because a single sweet potato big enough to carry 78 g would be about 390 g raw. The yogurt-and-blue-cheese drizzle instead of ranch is what leaves room for them.

name: Sheet-Pan Chicken Fajitas + Tortillas & Rice
ing: chicken breast 99 g; corn tortillas 52 g; white rice dry 50 g; bell pepper 100 g; onion 60 g; olive oil 7 g; pico de gallo 50 g; avocado 51 g; cheddar 10 g; greek yogurt nonfat 30 g
steps: Oven 450 °F — hotter than usual, because fajita vegetables want char, not steam.
Peppers, onion and sliced chicken tossed in oil, chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder and oregano. Spread across two pans rather than crowding one. Roast 18–20 min, tossing once.
Rice on alongside.
Warm the tortillas directly over a gas flame or on the Blackstone, 20 seconds a side. Lime over everything at the end.
store: Filling holds 4 days. Assemble fresh.

name: Teriyaki Salmon & Broccoli Rice Bowl
ing: salmon 124 g; jasmine rice dry 58 g; broccoli 150 g; soy sauce low sodium 25 g; honey 16 g; ginger 6 g; garlic 6 g; cornstarch 5 g; sesame oil 4 g; sesame seeds 4 g; scallions 10 g; edamame frozen 70 g
steps: Rice on. Broccoli roasted at 425 °F for 15 min, or steamed 5.

Reduce the teriyaki before it goes near the fish: soy, honey, ginger, garlic and the cornstarch slurry simmered 2–3 min until it coats a spoon. Glazing with unreduced sauce is why home teriyaki turns watery.
Salmon skin-side down in a hot pan 4 min, flip 2–3 min, brushing with the glaze in the last minute so the sugar does not burn.
Sesame seeds and scallion over.
Edamame steamed from frozen and tipped over at the end with the sesame seeds.
store: Fridge 3 days.
note: Different enough from D12 to run both in a month — that one is cold and spicy, this is hot and sweet.

name: Chicken Parmesan with Spaghetti
ing: chicken breast 70 g; panko 16 g; egg 15 g; spaghetti dry 72 g; marinara 130 g; mozzarella 20 g; parmesan 8 g; olive oil 8 g; broccoli 150 g
steps: Butterfly and pound the breasts to an even 1.5 cm. Even thickness matters more than thinness — the coating burns before a thick end cooks.
Flour, egg, panko. Shallow-fry in the oil 3 min a side until deep gold, then transfer to a baking dish.
Sauce and cheese on top, oven 400 °F, 10 min to melt. Do not sauce it before it goes in the pan — that is how the crust goes soft.
Spaghetti al dente, tossed with the remaining marinara.
Broccoli roasted alongside the cutlet for the last 12 min, or blanched in the pasta water. Chicken parm and spaghetti alone is 5.1 g of fibre.
store: Fridge 3 days. Reheat the cutlet in the oven, never the microwave.
note: Your cutlet is small — 50 g cooked. Chicken parm is normally 200 g of chicken under cheese, and even at a 37 P dinner slot that arithmetic does not work. The pasta is the meal here.

name: Blackstone Chicken Quesadillas + Mexican Rice
base: 90 g flour tortillas + 84 g cooked rice
ing: chicken breast 75 g; flour tortillas 90 g; cheddar 20 g; white rice dry 28 g; crushed tomatoes 40 g; onion 30 g; bell pepper 50 g; olive oil 4 g; greek yogurt nonfat 40 g; pico de gallo 40 g; black beans canned 50 g
steps: Mexican rice: toast the dry rice in a little oil 2 min until it smells nutty, then add the crushed tomato, stock and cumin and cook covered 18 min. Toasting first is the whole difference.
Griddle the diced chicken with peppers and onion, 8 min.
Tortilla down on the Blackstone, cheese, filling, cheese, fold. Cheese on both sides of the filling — it is the glue. 2–3 min a side, pressed.
Black beans warmed and drained well, spread inside the quesadilla with the chicken. Wet beans make a soggy tortilla — drain them properly.
store: Fridge 3 days. Re-crisp in a dry pan.

name: Shrimp Scampi with Linguine
ing: shrimp 100 g; linguine dry 92 g; butter 8 g; olive oil 11 g; garlic 10 g; white wine 30 g; lemon juice 15 g; parmesan 10 g; cherry tomatoes 80 g; spinach 40 g; broccolini 150 g
steps: Pasta into heavily salted water. Reserve 150 ml of the water before draining — the starch in it is what makes the sauce a sauce instead of oil.
Garlic gently in the oil and butter, 90 seconds, no colour. Burnt garlic ruins scampi.
Wine in, reduce by half, 2 min. Tomatoes, then shrimp, 2 min a side.
Pasta straight from the pot into the pan with a splash of the water, spinach folded through, lemon and parmesan off the heat.
Broccolini blanched 2 min in the pasta water, then into the pan with the shrimp for the last minute.
store: Fridge 2 days, and it is noticeably better fresh.
note: Cook this on a night you are both home.

name: Turkey Sloppy Joes with Oven Fries
ing: ground turkey 93/7 124 g; burger bun 60 g; ketchup 30 g; tomato paste 15 g; brown sugar 6 g; onion 40 g; bell pepper 40 g; potato 175 g; olive oil 7 g; cheddar 12 g
steps: Fries first: cut, soak 10 min in cold water and dry thoroughly. Wet fries steam instead of crisping. Oil, salt, 425 °F for 25 min, flipping once.
Brown the turkey with the onion and pepper, 8 min. Tomato paste 2 min.
Ketchup, brown sugar, Worcestershire, mustard powder and 60 ml water. Simmer 10 min until it holds on a spoon.
Toast the buns cut-side down in a dry pan. Cheddar on the hot meat.
store: The meat holds 4 days and freezes 3 months. Fries do not keep.

name: Beef & Broccoli Stir Fry with Rice
ing: sirloin steak 107 g; jasmine rice dry 54 g; broccoli 180 g; soy sauce low sodium 25 g; oyster sauce 20 g; honey 10 g; cornstarch 6 g; sesame oil 9 g; cashews 12 g; garlic 8 g; ginger 6 g; scallions 15 g; sugar snap peas 80 g
steps: Freeze the beef 15 minutes and slice it against the grain as thinly as you can — frozen, it cuts like paper. Toss with half the cornstarch.
Rice on. Broccoli blanched 2 min and shocked cold, so it finishes crisp in the wok rather than steaming.
Sauce: soy, oyster, honey, remaining cornstarch, 60 ml water.
Wok on high with half the sesame oil. Beef in one layer, 60 seconds untouched, toss 1 min, remove — it finishes in the sauce.
Garlic and ginger 30 seconds, broccoli 2 min, beef back, sauce in, toss 60–90 seconds to gloss. Cashews and scallion off the heat.
Snap peas into the wok with the broccoli — 60 seconds, they want to stay loud.
store: Fridge 3 days.
note: On a long-run Saturday, take the sesame oil to 15 g rather than 9 — that extra 6 g is what brings the day's fat to target.

name: Garlic Butter Steak Bites & Crispy Potatoes
ing: sirloin steak 108 g; potato 375 g; butter 8 g; olive oil 6 g; garlic 12 g; parmesan 10 g; green beans 130 g
steps: Potatoes: par-boil 8 min, drain, and shake them hard in the dry pan to rough up the edges. Those torn edges are what go crisp. Oil, 425 °F for 25 min or air fryer 20 min.
Green beans in for the last 12 min.
Steak bites: pan or Blackstone screaming hot, cubes dried on paper towel, in one layer, 90 seconds without moving, then toss 60–90 seconds.
Butter, garlic and parsley in at the very end, off the heat — 30 seconds, no more. Parmesan over the potatoes.
store: Fridge 3 days. Potatoes re-crisp in the air fryer.

name: Blackstone Philly Cheesesteak + Oven Fries
base: 100 g hoagie roll + 70 g oven fries
ing: sirloin steak 96 g; hoagie roll 100 g; provolone 18 g; green bell pepper 80 g; onion 80 g; olive oil 10 g; potato 90 g
steps: Fries first: cut, soak 10 min in cold water, dry thoroughly. Oil, salt, 425 °F for 25 min, flipping once.
Freeze the steak 15 minutes and slice it as thinly as you can against the grain — that is the whole difference between a cheesesteak and a beef sandwich.
Blackstone to medium-high. Peppers and onions in the oil, 6–7 min until soft and browning. Push aside.
Steak onto the bare griddle, 90 seconds without touching it, then chop and toss with the vegetables, 2 min more. Provolone laid over the pile, lid or a splash of water for 60 seconds to melt.
Split and toast the rolls cut-side down in the griddle fat, 45 seconds. Scoop the pile straight in.
store: Eat fresh. The steak-and-pepper mix holds 2 days; fries do not keep.
note: Untested — cooked once and not yet judged. The roll carries 52 g of carbohydrate on its own, which is why the fries alongside stay small. 90 g of raw potato is a small handful and that is correct.

name: French Onion Smothered Chicken + Garlic Mash
ing: chicken breast 89 g; potato 275 g; onion 150 g; gruyere 15 g; butter 12 g; olive oil 4 g; all-purpose flour 4 g; chicken stock 100 g; milk 2% 50 g; garlic 6 g; green beans 150 g
steps: Onions first — they are the recipe and they cannot be rushed under about 25 minutes. Slice thin, into a wide pan with the olive oil and half the butter over medium-low. Stir every few minutes: translucent at 10, gold at 18, deep brown and jammy at 25–30. If they are browning at 8 minutes the heat is too high and you are frying, not caramelising.
Potatoes peeled, cut into even 4 cm chunks, into cold salted water, brought to a boil, 18–20 min to falling apart. Starting them cold is what stops the outsides going gluey before the middles cook.
Butterfly the chicken into even cutlets, season, sear in a separate pan 4–5 min a side to 165 °F. Set aside to rest.
Flour stirred into the onions, 1 min, then stock and Worcestershire. Simmer 5 min to a gravy. Chicken back in, cheese over, lid on 3 min to melt.

Mash: drain the potatoes and let them steam dry in the pan for 2 minutes before anything goes in — this is what keeps mash from being watery. Warm milk, remaining butter, grated raw garlic, salt. Green beans steamed or roasted 12 min.
store: Fridge 4 days. Mash reheats with a splash of milk. Freezes poorly — eat it in the week.
note: Untested. The mash is the point: 275 g of raw potato carries 48 g of carbohydrate in a form you will actually finish, where the same carbohydrate as roasted wedges is a much bigger-looking plate. You had no mashed-potato dish in the library at all, which is an odd gap for someone whose only structural shortfall is starch.

name: Chicken Caesar Pasta Salad

Toss pasta, kale, tomatoes and chicken. Romaine and croutons in a separate cup, added at lunch.

name: Chicken Gnocchi Soup

Gnocchi straight in from the packet, 3–4 min until they float. They thicken the soup as they cook; that is the trick, and it is why no extra starch is needed.
Spinach folded through for the last minute. Parmesan at the table, sourdough for dipping.

name: Loaded Broccoli-Cheddar Chicken Potato
